bundles.evidenceText: a belief is rational then if and only if that belief is in accordance with the reason and evidence that's available to the believer
bundles.rationale: The move defines rational belief by conformity to the believer's available reason and evidence, but it does not apply that standard to evidence for or against theism. This definition can remain true whether theistic belief is rational or irrational, so no bridge receives exact contact. The nearest competitor, support for the pro motion bridge, is excluded because the complete conclusion that belief in the specified God is irrational is not asserted.

bundles.evidenceText: my theodicy provides a possible account but mere possibility doesn't imply high probability
bundles.rationale: The move argues by the evil-God parity that constructing a merely possible explanation does not make belief in such a deity probable or rational. This supports the pro subsidiary-1 bridge that merely possible theodicies do not overcome apparently gratuitous suffering. The proposition cannot remain true without strengthening that bridge's stated insufficiency inference. Pro-motion support is the nearest competitor, but the move advances this specific evil-and-theodicy premise rather than the complete motion conclusion.

bundles.evidenceText: most Christians let alone Muslims and Jews can't even agree on what's necessary for salvation
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that salvation carries grave consequences while sincere religious communities cannot agree on its necessary conditions. That proposition supports the pro subsidiary-2 bridge that an all-loving God would not attach grave eternal consequences to conditions people cannot reliably identify. Its truth makes that bridge more credible. Support for the pro central bridge is the nearest competitor, but the contact is specifically with salvation confusion rather than the route's broader evidential balance.

bundles.evidenceText: of those that are nevertheless convinced of its existence they don't agree on what it looks like what it's made of or where it's located
bundles.rationale: The move says an all-loving, all-powerful God imposes an elusive salvific hoop, believers disagree about its nature, and those unable to perceive it face eternal punishment. This supports the pro subsidiary-2 proposition concerning severe consequences attached to unreliable salvation conditions, and its truth directly strengthens that bridge. Pro-central support is excluded as the nearest competitor because the expressed reason is the narrower salvation-confusion claim, not the full weighing of all routes.

bundles.evidenceText: if God exists there is an intelligent Creator behind it all and we have good reason therefore to trust in the intelligence of our minds
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that unguided physical origins undermine trust in cognition, whereas an intelligent creator supplies a basis for trusting minds and the universe's intelligibility. This is support for the con subsidiary-1 bridge, and the proposition's truth directly increases that bridge's credibility. Con-central support is the nearest competitor, but the move supplies only the specific argument from reason rather than the combined case from reason, design, morality, and replies to suffering.

bundles.evidenceText: natural selection does not um directly select for True beliefs but rather for advantageous behaviors
bundles.rationale: The move argues that unguided natural selection favors advantageous behavior rather than truth and contrasts this with God-guided evolution aimed at rational knowledge. This supports the con subsidiary-1 bridge about naturalism undermining cognitive trust while a creator grounds it. The proposition cannot remain true without strengthening that comparison. Con-central support is excluded because no combined inference from design, morality, and suffering is expressed.

bundles.evidenceText: the reason this fine-tuning argument points so powerfully towards the existence of God
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that extremely precise life-permitting physical constants are practically impossible under chance and indicate a super-intellect. This supports the con subsidiary-2 bridge that life-permitting conditions are substantially more probable under intelligent design than unguided chance. The proposition directly raises that bridge's credibility. Con-central support is the nearest competitor, but this move presents only the fine-tuning component and not the cumulative route.

bundles.evidenceText: the existence of this objective moral law points us to the existence of God as the only good explanation
bundles.rationale: The move contends that objective moral law requires explanation, is difficult to derive from an impersonal universe, and points to God. This supports the con subsidiary-3 bridge that objective obligations are hard to ground impersonally but intelligible when grounded in God. Its truth directly strengthens that exact inference. Con-central support is excluded as the nearest competitor because the move states the moral component alone, not the combined cumulative case.

bundles.evidenceText: even if we accept it that atheism is irrational the first thing to note is that that's not an argument in favor of theism
bundles.rationale: The move denies that undermining atheism establishes theism, disputes the identification of atheism with naturalism, and questions why evolution would favor costly false beliefs. These propositions attack the con subsidiary-1 inference from unguided evolution to cognitive unreliability and then to God. They cannot remain true without weakening that bridge. Attack on the con motion bridge is excluded because the criticism targets this specific argument from reason, not the complete cumulative conclusion.

bundles.evidenceText: evolution is not going to select for things that are false and inaccurate about the world because it's entirely costly
bundles.rationale: The move argues that evolution selects broadly accurate world-directed cognition because false and inaccurate beliefs are costly, while allowing limited error. This attacks the con subsidiary-1 premise that unguided evolution leaves no rational confidence that minds track truth. The proposition directly lowers that bridge's credibility. Attack on the con central bridge is excluded because the move does not address fine-tuning, morality, or suffering and therefore does not attack the combined case.

bundles.evidenceText: they are geared primarily towards understanding the universe around us
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that, on the Christian view, minds are produced by intelligence and oriented primarily toward truth and an intelligible universe, whereas unguided evolution primarily serves reproductive success. This supports the con subsidiary-1 bridge and makes its creator-versus-naturalism comparison more credible. Con-central support is excluded because the proposition concerns only the rational-minds component, not the combined design, morality, and suffering inference.

bundles.evidenceText: you suffer from an equally irrational standpoint of what you accuse the naturalist of
bundles.rationale: The move argues that appeals to God's mysterious, undisclosed reasoning leave the theist with the same epistemic problem alleged against naturalism, so the comparison cannot favor God. This attacks the con subsidiary-1 inference that a creator uniquely provides a rational basis for cognitive trust. Its truth weakens that bridge directly. Con-motion attack is excluded as the nearest competitor because the expressed criticism is confined to the argument from reason rather than the cumulative conclusion.

bundles.evidenceText: I don't think it's a um it's a defeater
bundles.rationale: The move concedes that suffering is strong counterevidence but expressly denies that it defeats belief in an all-powerful, all-loving God and says responsive arguments exist. This attacks the pro subsidiary-1 bridge's claim that apparently gratuitous suffering and merely possible theodicies prevent rational belief. That denial directly limits the bridge's force. Support for the con central bridge is excluded because the move directly answers the narrower suffering bridge without invoking the full cumulative positive case.

bundles.evidenceText: I don't think an atheistic belief can affirm that instinct
bundles.rationale: The move claims that the intuition that suffering makes the world other than it ought to be is affirmed by Christianity but cannot be affirmed by an atheistic universe of blind indifference. This supports the con subsidiary-3 proposition that objective moral normativity is difficult under an impersonal universe but intelligible with God. Its truth strengthens that comparison. Attack on pro subsidiary-1 is excluded because the move does not explain why suffering serves a greater good or rebut its probability.

bundles.evidenceText: any weighing up of things must take into account God's resources of what he's able to do in an afterlife
bundles.rationale: The move argues that assessing earthly suffering must include an eternal future in which God can remedy loss and wipe away tears. This attacks the pro subsidiary-1 inference that observed suffering serving no apparent greater good makes belief in an all-loving, all-powerful God irrational. The proposition, if true, weakens that inference by adding a proposed compensating good. Con-central support is excluded because the move is a direct response to the narrower suffering bridge, not a statement of the cumulative case.

bundles.evidenceText: there are very respected arguments in the literature such of the argument for the best of all possible Worlds free will defense Soul making theodicy
bundles.rationale: The move rejects the dismissal of theodicies as invented stories, identifies free-will and soul-making responses, and adds that God enters and accompanies human suffering. This attacks the pro subsidiary-1 claim that merely possible theodicies cannot preserve rational belief despite apparently gratuitous evil. Those propositions weaken that bridge if true. Con-central support is excluded because the move directly contests the suffering objection rather than supplying the full cumulative inference.

bundles.evidenceText: why we have these intuitions in general very much explained for us being a social species
bundles.rationale: The move offers social evolution as an explanation for moral concern, sacrifice, religious motifs, and the intuition that the world ought to be different. Because it directly answers the claim that atheism cannot explain moral normativity, it attacks the con subsidiary-3 bridge that moral obligations are difficult to ground in an impersonal universe. Its truth weakens that bridge. Support for pro subsidiary-3 is excluded under the direct-attack rule: although an evolutionary alternative is offered, the expressed target is the con moral inference.

bundles.evidenceText: if God commands us to do things because they are good then the good obviously exists independent of God
bundles.rationale: The move presents the Euthyphro dilemma: goodness either exists independently of God or reduces to arbitrary divine command, which would not be morality. This attacks the con subsidiary-3 inference that objective morality is intelligibly grounded in God. The proposition directly undermines that grounding claim. Support for pro subsidiary-3 is excluded as the nearest competitor because the move is framed as a direct objection to the con moral bridge rather than as a general evolutionary account of morality.

bundles.evidenceText: moral standards that you're holding them up against are probably the moral standards that have historically resulted from the influence of the Bible
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that biblical influence historically promoted equal dignity and helped shape the moral standards used to criticize religion. That historical causal proposition can remain true even if God does not exist and even if objective morality is not metaphysically grounded in God, so it contacts no bridge. The nearest competitor is support for con subsidiary-3, but historical conduct and doctrinal influence do not establish that bridge's proposition about the grounding of objective obligations.

bundles.evidenceText: objective goodness from where I sit is rooted not in some abstract concept that floats around in space but in the person who created everything
bundles.rationale: The move answers the Euthyphro dilemma by asserting that God neither follows an external good nor arbitrarily invents it; God is the personal source in whom objective goodness is rooted. This supports the con subsidiary-3 bridge that objective morality is intelligible when goodness is grounded in God. Its truth directly strengthens that proposition. Con-central support is excluded because the move supplies only the moral-grounding component rather than the cumulative route.

bundles.evidenceText: you are stuck with hea having to admit that morality exists independent of God or the morality isn't morality
bundles.rationale: The move argues that identifying God with goodness merely restates the Euthyphro dilemma: goodness is either independent of God or defined by God and therefore non-moral command. This attacks the con subsidiary-3 claim that grounding goodness in God makes objective morality intelligible. The proposition directly weakens that bridge. Support for pro subsidiary-3 is excluded under the direct-attack rule because the move specifically challenges the con moral-grounding answer rather than advancing the pro bridge's broader evolutionary account.

bundles.evidenceText: we're very fortunate in the sense that we live in a time and an age where Evolution has made it very clear that if God exists he chose to use Evolution
bundles.rationale: The move argues that biological complexity once made a creator hypothesis rational in the absence of a natural account, but evolution now explains that apparent design and at most leaves God as using evolution. This supports the pro subsidiary-3 bridge that alternative evolutionary explanations undercut apparent design as an identifier of the proposed God. Its truth strengthens that exact proposition. Attack on con subsidiary-2 is excluded because that bridge concerns cosmic life-permitting constants, whereas this move concerns biological complexity.
